chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Musa ibn Jafar al-Baghdadi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I heard Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام saying regarding the Maghrib: when the disc disappears, it is the time of salat (prayer) and iftar.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), here referring to Maghrib prayer
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the Maghrib time and prayer at sunset
key_terms.تَوَارَى: became hidden or disappeared from sight
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the appointed time or legal commencement time

ai.seo_question: When does the time of Maghrib salat (prayer) and iftar begin according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the time of Maghrib begins when the sun’s disc disappears. It also indicates that this moment marks both the time for salat (prayer) and for iftar in fasting.
